title: Georgia's 3rd Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 general election for Georgia's 3rd Congressional District pits first-term Republican incumbent Brian Jack against Democratic nominee Maura Keller. The district covers 15 counties in west-central Georgia, including parts of the Atlanta suburbs and rural communities. Jack, a former White House Political Director under President Trump, won the seat in 2024 with 66.3% of the vote after the retirement of longtime Rep. Drew Ferguson. Keller, a retired U.S. Army lieutenant colonel and former VA health worker, defeated George Melville Johnson in the May 19 Democratic primary and is running on a platform of affordability, healthcare access, and veterans' issues in a district rated Solidly Republican by nonpartisan analysts.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for the 2026 general election in Georgia's 3rd Congressional District. The Cook Political Report rated the race as 'Solidly Republican' prior to the primary.

candidates.name: Brian Jack
candidates.summary: Incumbent U.S. Representative Brian Jack is seeking re-election to a second term representing Georgia's 3rd Congressional District. A longtime Trump administration aide who served as White House Political Director from 2019 to 2021, Jack won the open seat in 2024 with 66.3% of the vote after running unopposed in the 2026 Republican primary. He emphasizes border security, tax cuts, energy independence, and conservative judicial appointments.

candidates.name: Maura Keller
candidates.summary: Maura Keller is the Democratic nominee for Georgia's 3rd Congressional District. A retired U.S. Army lieutenant colonel with 26 years of service and a former VA health worker, Keller defeated George Melville Johnson in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary with 60.8% of the vote. Her campaign focuses on affordability, healthcare access, veterans' advocacy, and rural issues. Keller previously ran as the Democratic nominee for this seat in 2024, losing to Brian Jack.

forecast.rationale: No general-election polling exists for this race, which tempers confidence. However, the available structural indicators are overwhelming: first-term Republican incumbent Brian Jack won the open seat with 66.3% in 2024, the district is rated Solidly Republican by nonpartisan analysts (Cook Political Report), Keller is the same Democratic nominee who lost to Jack in 2024, and Jack ran unopposed in his primary. The district's 15 counties in west-central Georgia reliably favor Republicans at the federal level. Absent any contrary data, Republican hold is extremely probable, consistent with a safe-r rating.
